claim: For the equiprobable binary two-qubit ensemble used by Chitambar and Hsieh to separate two-way from one-way LOCC discrimination, and for their explicit one-parameter two-way protocol with measurement strength \(p\in[0,1]\), the error probability \[E(p)=\frac{1}{16}\left(6-\sqrt{4-3p}-\sqrt{4+5p}\right)\]has the unique global minimizer \[p_*=\frac{8}{15}.\]The exact protocol minimum is \[E_*=\frac{3}{8}-\frac{\sqrt{15}}{15}=0.1168011102528\ldots,\]while the optimal one-way LOCC error is \(E_{\to}=1/8\). Hence this published two-way witness has the exact maximal error advantage \[E_{\to}-E_*=\frac{4\sqrt{15}-15}{60}=0.00819888974716\ldots>0.\]The source's separable-operation optimum is \((3-\sqrt5)/8\), so this explicit protocol remains above it by \[\frac{\sqrt5}{8}-\frac{\sqrt{15}}{15}>0.\]The claim optimizes only the source's displayed one-parameter protocol family; it does not claim the globally optimal two-way LOCC error.

integrity.computational_dependence: none for the proof; high-precision evaluation and a dense grid are supplementary checks
integrity.novelty_scope: Unique closed-form optimizer, exact minimum error, and exact maximal one-way advantage within the source's explicit binary two-way LOCC witness family.
integrity.prior_work_preserved: The ensemble, adaptive protocol, analytic error formula, optimal one-way error, and separable-operation benchmark are credited to the cited prior work.

scientific_limitations: The result optimizes only the one-parameter two-way LOCC protocol explicitly displayed in the source.
It does not determine the globally optimal finite-round or unrestricted two-way LOCC error.
The one-way and separable-operation benchmark values are prior results and are not re-claimed.
An equivalent closed-form simplification may exist under a different parametrization in literature not surfaced by the searches.
title: Exact sharp calibration of the binary two-way LOCC hierarchy witness
